summaries.demographer: Alan Russell is a 52-year-old white, non-Hispanic married man living in owner-occupied housing in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan, with his wife Sarah and teenage son Jacob, while his daughter Emily is away at Michigan State (Q05, Q51, Q58, Q88-Q89). He has a master's degree and works as a public school STEM teacher, placing him in a stable upper-middle-class professional household with two education-sector incomes (Q65, Q74, Q90). His life-course profile shows suburban Detroit roots, long-term marriage, active parenting, aging-parent responsibilities, and strong local attachment (Q01, Q35, Q87, Q97).
summaries.behavioral_economist: Alan is a planner with relatively low financial impulsivity: he budgets with spreadsheets, uses automatic savings, maintains emergency reserves, and delays discretionary purchases when expenses rise (Q57, Q60-Q62, Q82). His choices show long time horizons around retirement, college funding, health maintenance, and career development, while still allowing modest experiential spending such as travel and hobbies (Q62, Q83, Q108). He responds to uncertainty through preparation and information-gathering rather than risk-taking, visible in his career decision, household finances, and health routines (Q02, Q31-Q33, Q61). Peer and identity incentives matter most in education, family, and civic service rather than consumption status (Q23, Q65, Q109).
summaries.political_scientist: Alan is a consistent voter and center-left Democrat whose political identity is anchored in public education, science, institutional trust, and local civic engagement (Q23-Q25, Q95-Q96). He supports school funding campaigns, public libraries, vaccination, and evidence-based policy, reflecting high trust in professional and public institutions when they are accountable (Q23, Q41-Q42, Q103-Q104). His views on race and policing are sympathetic to Black Lives Matter concerns, though his response is more deliberative and institutional than activist (Q26-Q30). He is attached to community institutions but critical of affluent suburban bubbles and unequal opportunity structures (Q08, Q28).
summaries.psychologist: Alan presents as conscientious, pragmatic, intellectually curious, and somewhat anxious under load, with stress expressed through overplanning, late-night work, and responsibility-taking (Q15, Q43-Q45). His self-concept centers on being useful, steady, competent, and service-oriented, especially as a teacher, husband, father, and community member (Q65, Q108-Q109). He copes through walking, cooking, guitar, family conversations, and structured problem-solving rather than substances or emotional disclosure online (Q38-Q40, Q43, Q49-Q50). Relationally, he maintains a small stable circle, values family rituals, and shows reflective awareness of privilege, aging, and limits (Q05-Q08, Q35, Q83).
